method: Sep 1 extension after reviewing the tactical-caution, anti-fiat, TTWO and critical-mineral source set plus primary/authoritative follow-up. Current Research Scores reflect durable business/thesis quality plus current evidence; immediate Watchlist scores separately penalize hostile rates, crowding, technical location, leverage and portfolio overlap.
regime: Structural scarcity and monetary-hedge themes are strengthening, but the next 2-3 weeks remain tactically fragile because real/nominal yields are high, September Fed-hike risk is live and momentum/positioning are unstable beneath the indices.

newIdeas.name: SPDR Gold MiniShares Trust
newIdeas.thesis: Clean physical-gold exposure with a low expense ratio. Best suited to portfolio-level fiscal/geopolitical/debasement hedging without mine operating risk.
newIdeas.catalysts: Falling real yields, weaker USD, central-bank purchases, fiscal stress, Treasury-market intervention and geopolitical escalation.
newIdeas.risks: Delivered Fed hikes, higher real yields, stronger USD and crowded anti-fiat positioning.
newIdeas.researchNote: Structural thesis remains strong, but immediate entry score is lower than structural conviction until the Warsh/Fed and real-yield path clears.

newIdeas.name: Agnico Eagle Mines
newIdeas.theme: High-quality gold miner · low balance-sheet risk
newIdeas.thesis: Best-quality miner in the current gold sleeve: strong production, low AISC relative to realised gold, very high FCF and net cash reduce the usual miner fragility.
newIdeas.catalysts: Gold-margin expansion, production execution, shareholder returns and sustained central-bank/anti-fiat demand.
newIdeas.risks: Gold pullback, mining-cost inflation, operational disruptions and equity-beta drawdowns during risk-off.
newIdeas.researchNote: Preferred miner when the gold thesis is intact but equity volatility is elevated.

newIdeas.name: Kinross Gold
newIdeas.thesis: Higher operating leverage than physical gold with attractive valuation and strong FCF. Less pristine than AEM operationally, but better upside asymmetry if gold resumes higher.
newIdeas.catalysts: Gold-price recovery, FCF growth, buybacks/dividends and reserve/production execution.
newIdeas.risks: AISC inflation, gold correction and greater equity beta than GLDM/WPM.
newIdeas.researchNote: AEM is the better company; KGC may be the better stock at the right entry.

newIdeas.name: Wheaton Precious Metals
newIdeas.thesis: Streaming model captures precious-metal upside while avoiding much of the direct diesel/labour/capex inflation that can hit miners.
newIdeas.catalysts: Higher gold/silver prices, new streams and production growth at partner mines.
newIdeas.risks: Premium valuation, counterparty/mine execution risk and precious-metal drawdowns.
newIdeas.researchNote: Particularly attractive when gold rises alongside oil/labour costs.

newIdeas.name: VanEck Gold Miners ETF
newIdeas.thesis: Diversified miner basket removes single-mine/company risk while retaining operating leverage to gold.
newIdeas.catalysts: Broad miner margin expansion and renewed gold momentum.
newIdeas.risks: Equity beta, cost inflation and crowded miner positioning.
newIdeas.researchNote: Use when diversified miner torque is desired instead of selecting individual operators.

newIdeas.name: Newmont
newIdeas.thesis: Large-scale gold exposure with useful copper optionality, but operating-cost and execution variability keep it below AEM/KGC in the current hierarchy.
newIdeas.catalysts: Gold/copper prices, portfolio optimization and capital returns.
newIdeas.risks: Diesel/labour inflation, mine execution and asset-specific disruption.
newIdeas.researchNote: Good diversified miner, not the first incremental gold dollar.

newIdeas.name: iShares Gold Trust
newIdeas.thesis: Clean physical-gold exposure, but GLDM is preferred for a low-cost long-term sleeve while GLD retains superior trading liquidity.
newIdeas.catalysts: Same gold macro drivers as GLDM.
newIdeas.risks: Higher real yields and stronger USD.
newIdeas.researchNote: Useful alternative, but largely redundant beside GLDM.

newIdeas.name: SPDR Gold Shares
newIdeas.thesis: Deep liquidity and options market make GLD ideal for tactical implementation; GLDM remains preferable for lower-cost long-term holding.
newIdeas.catalysts: Same gold macro drivers as GLDM.
newIdeas.risks: Higher fee than GLDM and the same real-yield/USD headwinds.
newIdeas.researchNote: Trading tool more than preferred long-term core.

newIdeas.name: VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF
newIdeas.thesis: High convexity to a gold/miner breakout but much weaker balance sheets, liquidity and execution than the senior-miner sleeve.
newIdeas.catalysts: Sustained gold breakout and risk-on flows into miners.
newIdeas.risks: Financing/dilution, mine execution, liquidity and violent drawdowns.
newIdeas.researchNote: Not a core Power Stack allocation under the current bond regime.

newIdeas.name: Bitcoin
newIdeas.thesis: Institutional and regulatory infrastructure are improving and fiscal/debasement narratives support the medium term, but BTC remains much more sensitive than gold to real yields and tightening liquidity.
newIdeas.catalysts: ETF inflows, weaker real yields/USD, regulatory clarity and renewed liquidity expansion.
newIdeas.risks: Fed tightening, ETF outflows, leverage liquidations and risk-off liquidity contraction.
newIdeas.researchNote: Medium-term constructive; immediate buy score is lower while the Fed-hike/real-yield regime remains hostile.

newIdeas.name: Coinbase Global
newIdeas.thesis: Best fundamental crypto-equity expression: growing trading share, subscription/services and USDC economics reduce dependence on simple BTC spot-volume beta.
newIdeas.catalysts: Crypto volumes, market-share gains, USDC/stablecoin growth, subscription revenue and regulatory clarity.
newIdeas.risks: Crypto drawdown, trading-volume collapse, regulation and high equity beta.
newIdeas.researchNote: Preferred crypto equity on risk-adjusted fundamentals; do not chase after the August rebound.

newIdeas.name: Strategy
newIdeas.thesis: High-convexity BTC exposure layered with debt, preferreds, ATM issuance and capital-structure reflexivity. Can outperform dramatically in a liquidity boom but has materially worse downside mechanics than BTC itself.
newIdeas.catalysts: BTC breakout, higher mNAV/premium and accretive capital raising.
newIdeas.risks: BTC drawdown, mNAV compression, common dilution, preferred obligations and financing-cost pressure.
newIdeas.researchNote: Treat as a capital-structure trade, not a substitute for BTC.

newIdeas.name: Solstice Advanced Materials
newIdeas.theme: Recent Honeywell spin · UF6 + refrigerants + specialty materials
newIdeas.thesis: One of the strongest post-spin pure plays: sole US UF6 supplier, refrigerants/electronic materials, 25%+ EBITDA margin, raised 2026 guidance and a cleaner balance-sheet path after abandoning the expensive Element deal.
newIdeas.catalysts: UF6 expansion, nuclear backlog, refrigerant/electronic-material growth, $500m buyback and standalone execution.
newIdeas.risks: Post-cancellation price gap, specialty-chemical cyclicality, nuclear customer concentration and spin-off execution.
newIdeas.researchNote: Best new spin-off candidate for Power Stack because it overlaps nuclear fuel, cooling/refrigerants and electronics while already generating cash.

newIdeas.name: Qnity Electronics
newIdeas.thesis: Pure-play semiconductor materials exposure created from DuPont. Q2 sales +22%, adjusted earnings +53% and EBITDA +24% validate profitable AI/HPC semiconductor exposure despite a still-demanding multiple.
newIdeas.catalysts: AI/HPC wafer intensity, advanced packaging/interconnect demand, raised guidance and margin expansion.
newIdeas.risks: Semiconductor cycle, high valuation, China exposure and customer capex volatility.
newIdeas.researchNote: A better way to play AI semiconductor materials than another chip designer if entry valuation is disciplined.

newIdeas.name: L3Harris Technologies
newIdeas.theme: Defense + planned Missile Solutions IPO/value unlock
newIdeas.thesis: Record $42bn backlog and strong FCF support the parent while the planned Missile Solutions IPO creates a value-unlock catalyst around scarce solid-rocket-motor capacity.
newIdeas.catalysts: Missile Solutions IPO, DoW-backed capacity expansion, rearmament orders and backlog conversion.
newIdeas.risks: Leadership transition, IPO delay/valuation, program timing and government-budget exposure.
newIdeas.researchNote: The future Missile Solutions vehicle may become an unusually pure missile-rearmament asset; owning LHX now is the parent-company route to that catalyst.

newIdeas.name: Honeywell Aerospace
newIdeas.thesis: High-quality aerospace/defense installed-base and aftermarket exposure at a reasonable forward multiple, but the first standalone quarter included a material guidance cut that keeps it below LHX/SOLS/Q.
newIdeas.catalysts: Aftermarket growth, defense/space backlog conversion and standalone cost normalization.
newIdeas.risks: Further guidance cuts, supply constraints, separation costs and aviation-cycle exposure.
newIdeas.researchNote: Interesting after the June spin, but wait for proof that reduced 2026 guidance is the reset rather than the start of another downgrade cycle.

newIdeas.name: Honeywell Technologies
newIdeas.thesis: The remaining Honeywell is now a more focused automation company with improving segment margins, strong cash generation and less aerospace conglomerate noise.
newIdeas.catalysts: Process/industrial automation growth, margin expansion, FCF and portfolio simplification.
newIdeas.risks: Industrial slowdown, integration/divestiture execution and valuation.
newIdeas.researchNote: Worth monitoring as a cleaner automation compounder rather than a traditional conglomerate.

newThemes.name: Gold / Monetary Hedges
newThemes.summary: Gold, silver and BTC were August's clearest anti-fiat winners as fiscal credibility, Treasury intervention and geopolitical risk rose. The structural case is stronger, but Warsh's hawkish reaction and high real yields make immediate chase risk poor.
newThemes.whyNow: Gold gained roughly 10% in August and the fiscal/geopolitical hedge narrative is broadening, yet the September Fed meeting creates a near-term real-yield hurdle. The correct trade-off is accumulate quality on dips, not treat anti-fiat as a one-way momentum trade.
newThemes.marketTransmission: Falling real yields/USD and policy intervention lift gold first, then miners/streamers; delivered tightening or stronger real yields compress precious-metal multiples and usually hit BTC harder than physical gold.
newThemes.confirmation: Real yields roll over and gold reclaims the broken trend/high while miner FCF/AISC remain strong.
newThemes.invalidation: A sustained real-yield/USD breakout plus delivered Fed tightening causes gold and miners to lose major support.
newThemes.nextTest: NFP, CPI, Sep 16 Fed, US10Y/TIPS and gold ETF/CTA positioning.
newThemes.watchlistAction: Add GLDM/AEM/KGC/WPM/GDX to the research universe; favor GLDM/AEM on risk-adjusted quality and buy pullbacks rather than momentum.

newThemes.name: Crypto / Digital-Asset Liquidity
newThemes.summary: BTC had its strongest month since 2024 and regulatory/institutional infrastructure keeps improving, but the asset remains tightly exposed to real yields and liquidity. COIN fundamentals are improving faster than MSTR's risk-adjusted capital structure.
newThemes.whyNow: Bitcoin is holding below ~$80k after a ~25% August rally while Fed-hike odds and real yields are elevated. This is exactly the environment where the difference between clean BTC, operating crypto infrastructure and leveraged treasury structures matters.
newThemes.marketTransmission: Liquidity expansion and lower real yields can produce explosive BTC/COIN/MSTR upside; tightening hits MSTR first through mNAV/financing reflexivity, then COIN via activity beta, with BTC the cleanest asset-level exposure.
newThemes.confirmation: BTC closes above ~$81.3k with improving ETF flows while real yields stop rising and COIN activity remains strong.
newThemes.invalidation: BTC loses ~$68k alongside ETF outflows/liquidity deterioration or MSTR financing/mNAV stress accelerates.
newThemes.nextTest: Sep macro/Fed, BTC ETF flows, Coinbase activity and Strategy weekly capital-markets filings.
newThemes.watchlistAction: Prefer BTC/COIN to MSTR on risk-adjusted exposure under the current rates regime; keep MSTR speculative only.

newThemes.name: Western Critical-Mineral Sovereignty
newThemes.summary: Western governments are accelerating non-China critical-mineral supply chains while permitting/community friction raises the scarcity value of qualified producers and processors.
newThemes.whyNow: Canada's critical-mineral push, US/Japan price-floor support and new non-China processing projects show strategic policy becoming investable. The Ring of Fire story is broader critical minerals rather than a pure rare-earth deposit, so producer selection matters.
newThemes.marketTransmission: Government offtakes, floors and financing can improve economics for existing rare-earth processors while permitting delays increase strategic scarcity. Permanent magnets link the theme to defense, robotics, EVs and industrial automation.
newThemes.confirmation: Non-China producers show volume/profit growth and secure long-term floors/offtakes while downstream magnet capacity expands.
newThemes.invalidation: China pricing overwhelms Western support or projects remain permanently uneconomic despite subsidies.
newThemes.nextTest: MP/Lynas production and contracts, magnet-factory milestones, Canadian permitting and Malaysia processing plans.
newThemes.watchlistAction: Research MP and Lynas first; avoid speculative pre-revenue explorers until economics and permitting are proven.

newThemes.name: Corporate Breakups / Pure-Play Re-rating
newThemes.summary: Recent and upcoming separations are creating cleaner pure plays in seed genetics, nuclear materials, semiconductor materials, aerospace, automation and missile propulsion. This is not a blanket spin-off trade: execution quality and standalone economics dominate.
newThemes.whyNow: Vylor is due Oct 1; Honeywell's SOLS/HONA/HON breakup is now producing standalone data; Qnity is growing rapidly; L3Harris still plans a Missile Solutions IPO; Siemens Energy is preparing to deconsolidate Omterra.
newThemes.marketTransmission: Pure-play disclosure can unlock valuation and capital-allocation clarity, but spin-offs can also reveal stranded costs, leverage and weak standalone margins.
newThemes.confirmation: Standalone companies deliver better growth/margins/FCF than carve-out expectations without excessive leverage.
newThemes.invalidation: Repeated guidance cuts, stranded-cost inflation, leverage or failed capital allocation erase the pure-play benefit.
newThemes.nextTest: Vylor Investor Day Sep 15 / Oct 1 separation, HONA standalone execution, SOLS post-merger-cancel capital allocation, Missile Solutions IPO timing.
newThemes.watchlistAction: SOLS and LHX are the strongest incremental spin-off ideas now; Q is attractive on valuation discipline; HONA remains selective until guidance stabilises.
